title: Magnesium Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Magnesium Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Magnesium deficiency shows on the old leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Magnesium deficiency in plants starts on the old, lower leaves. Magnesium sits at the center of every chlorophyll molecule, so leaves cannot stay green or make food without it. It switches on many enzymes, helps move phosphorus through the plant, and helps carry sugars to where they are needed. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Tomato leaf yellow between green veins on an older, lower leaf: the magnesium shortage pattern

blocks.text: Magnesium moves readily from lower to upper leaves when the supply runs short. So the yellowing between the veins starts on the old, lower leaves and reaches the young ones only in bad cases.
Magnesium deficiency symptoms

Older leaves turn yellow, orange or bronze between the veins while the veins stay green. So corn and rice leaves look striped or beaded. As it gets worse, the yellow parts turn reddish purple and die, and old leaves may drop early. Rice leaves grow wavy and droopy and fill fewer, lighter grains. Sweet potato leaves turn reddish purple.
Magnesium deficiency by crop

Each crop shows it its own way. So find yours in the tables below, then open its page for the photo and the full fix, like the one for [magnesium in rice](/nutrient-deficiencies/rice-nutrient-deficiency#magnesium).

blocks.text: What causes magnesium deficiency

Acid, sandy soils hold little magnesium, and heavy rain leaches it down past the roots. Heavy doses of potash or ammonium fertilizer crowd it out at the roots. So does liming with plain lime instead of dolomite. Rainfed and upland fields that never get magnesium back slowly run out, and PCA surveys found magnesium short in some coconut areas.
How to be sure it is magnesium

Potassium shortage also starts on old leaves, but it burns the leaf edges instead of yellowing between the veins. Manganese shortage gives a similar pattern between the veins, but on the young leaves at the top. A soil test for exchangeable magnesium and pH at a DA Regional Soils Laboratory shows if the soil is short. A leaf tissue test confirms it, but take the same leaf at the same growth stage each time, because magnesium levels change with leaf age.
How to fix magnesium deficiency

On acid soils, dolomite is the cheapest fix, because it corrects the acidity and adds calcium and magnesium together. Where the pH is already right, or where heavy potash caused the shortage, use Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate) or kieserite. Let the soil test set the rate.
A magnesium nitrate spray at about 2 kg per 100 liters of water, every two weeks, is a typical rate in a Haifa vegetable guide. Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) also works as a foliar spray.

How to keep magnesium deficiency away

Lime acid fields with dolomite instead of plain lime, and keep potash in balance so it does not crowd out magnesium. Return straw and manure, and on sloping uplands control erosion so the topsoil and its magnesium stay put.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: True magnesium excess is rare in farm soils. Research finds crops grow well over a wide range of calcium to magnesium ratios. So there is no need to buy products sold to fix the ratio when the soil test shows both are adequate.

blocks.text: Magnesium deficiency questions

items.q: What does magnesium deficiency look like?
items.a: Old, lower leaves turn yellow, orange or reddish between the veins while the veins stay green. In corn and rice this shows as yellow stripes along the leaf.

items.q: What is the best fertilizer for magnesium deficiency?
items.a: Dolomite is the best value on acid soils because it also corrects the acidity. On soils that are not acid, use Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate) or kieserite.

items.q: Can I spray Epsom salt on my plants?
items.a: Yes. Magnesium sulfate works as a foliar spray. A Haifa vegetable guide uses magnesium nitrate at about 2 kg per 100 liters every two weeks. The spray helps the leaves, but dolomite or Epsom salt in the soil fixes the cause.

items.q: Why did my crop turn yellow between the veins after I added a lot of potash?
items.a: Heavy potash crowds out magnesium at the roots, mostly on sandy soils. Epsom salt is the best fix for a shortage caused this way, and next time keep the potash dose in balance.
